title: Stratum-Alpha (Chronos-Relay Protocol): Runtime Invariants and Algorithmic Bounds in Python
topic: A2A (Agent2Agent Protocol): Building Interoperable Aether-Vector Systems
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: The Stratum-Alpha (Chronos-Relay) Protocol implements a distributed agent-to-agent communication layer that preserves causal order through vector clocks while maintaining a height-balanced search tree for efficient message routing. We formalise the protocol's state machine, prove that the tree remains strictly height-balanced after each insertion or deletion, and show that message delivery satisfies the causal ordering invariant. The algorithm achieves $O(\log N)$ worst-case time for point and range queries, and $O(\log N)$ amortised time for node rebalancing, as established by classical amortised analysis \cite{Tarjan_1985_AmortizedComplexity}. The implementation is written in Python and is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/python-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261031_090115_a2a__agent2agent_protocol___bu}.
